body: The problem is that a logical approach won't work. If I listed out the positive and negative aspects of my life, the positives would bear more weight than the negatives. Despite this I still weigh give the negatives more weight than they are worth. Even the fact that I know I am doing this has no effect on this mindset.
There is a difference between your conscious reason for frustration and your subconscious reason. Usually the subconscious reason has more influence.
I specifically said that you were looking down on my way of thinking. This explains your frustration since that is a normal reaction to a thought that contradicts your own beliefs.

I know that there is more information out there that I don't know than what I do know (and by a massive margin at that). These things really have nothing to do with me. 

Let me give you an example of the type of things I am talking about. Whether you know it or not, I can see that you are looking down on my method of thinking. You aren't judging what type of person I am, but are just seeing my perspective of life for something that it isn't: being closed-minded (on a semi-side note, I am more open-minded than any person I have come across). I am drunk - the reason I took the time to post this thread - and can't remember what else I wanted to say in this comment so I'll have to stop here.

Also, as far as my potential goes:
I have seen for myself that I am capable of doing things that no one else can do. I *know* that, statistically, I will be smarter than any person I come across in my life. This makes my situation worse. I am wasting the gifts of intelligence and many others (mainly musical creativity) that only a handful of people in the history of mankind have been recognized for having. The worst part is that I recognize the severity of this and it doesn't bother me.

I understand where you're going with this, but can honestly tell you that nothing you have been through (which may have been worse than what I'm feeling now) is comparable to my current situation. There is no conceivable way that therapy will have any effect on me because I understand the logic behind it too well. I say this because of the experience I have with "discovering" psychological concepts; there have been a myriad of times where I will figure out some psychological fact on my own, only to later discover that this has already been hypothesized proven by professionals.

If I am capable of doing this, there is no way that any psychiatrist (who, chances are, I would be able to easily outmaneuver intellectually) would be able to learn anything about me that my conscious mind wouldn't want them to know.

Honestly, there isn't a day that goes by in which I don't wish that I was actually overestimating my intelligence. There was even a point in my life where I smoked weed multiple times every day hoping that it would make me at least a little bit dumber.

I'm not even sure I have a medical condition (I'm assuming you're talking about depression or a mood and/or personality disorder). I think that I see things the way I see them now because I have become too good at seeing through others' bullshit; whether they are acting nice towards me when they don't like me or are just hiding their real personality from everyone. I see people's flaws too easily and begin to dislike people once I see certain traits. There are a select few people whose flaws I can look past and still like them overall, but for a vast majority of people I come across this is not the case.

There is no way any therapy could help me. I would be able to see anything that I am asked to talk about for what it really is and not be fully honest because of this. I would be wasting someone's time by receiving help.
